workflow.name: Application overview → Evidence and functional catalog
workflow.description: Analyzes the current codebase and documentation to build an application overview, an evidence report, a plain-language summary and a functional catalog for subsequent workflows. Claude prepares the content, Codex verifies it independently, and a human approves the result.

nodes.title: Initial analysis
nodes.prompt:
Analyze all customer-provided material in Source for the application to modernize. Create EVIDENCE.md in the workspace root: application purpose, architecture, technologies, components, available information, completeness and reliability, size, integrations, risks, missing evidence and questions for the customer. Cite primary source paths and distinguish verified facts, inferences and unknowns. Ask Codex for an adversarial check when available; record whether that check actually occurred. Do not modify customer material or invent measurements, test results or approvals.

RERUN NOTE: if EVIDENCE.md already exists and is complete (application overview, architecture, inventory, business behavior, integrations, gaps and risks, customer questions, conclusions and a reproducible methodology note), verify that it is present and readable and reuse it without changes. Continue with SUMMARY.md and the functional catalog. Produce all documents in English.

nodes.title: Write SUMMARY.md
nodes.prompt: Create or overwrite SUMMARY.md in the workspace root: a plain-language summary of EVIDENCE.md. Describe the application's purpose, business areas, execution model, technologies, size, integrations, modernization uncertainties and outstanding customer questions. Derive every statement and number from EVIDENCE.md; verify numbers before writing and report discrepancies. Do not reuse counts, company names or business rules from another project. Clearly distinguish measured facts from estimates and unknowns. Include a provenance note referencing EVIDENCE.md and report independent review only if documented. Do not estimate effort or duration. Do not modify EVIDENCE.md or customer material. Write in English.

nodes.title: Functional catalog
nodes.prompt:
Create or overwrite FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md in the workspace root: a catalog of the application's functional chains to support modernization scoping and sequencing.

SOURCES: use EVIDENCE.md and SUMMARY.md for orientation, then inspect primary sources available in Source: flow maps, scheduler exports, jobs, commands, conditions, status and frequency; scripts and procedures; application source, build files and shared definitions; database schemas, SQL and load layouts; and customer documentation. Discover actual names, formats and counts from this project. Declare missing or ambiguous sources.

CATALOG UNIT: a functional chain is a set of jobs and components delivering a recognizable business outcome. Start from documented components and flows; split or merge only when supported by sources and explain each choice. Include isolated scheduler folders and components, assigning them to chains only when commands, scripts, files or tables support the association.

FOR EACH CHAIN: stable ID; name; business area; organizational scope; plain-language description (2–3 sentences); trigger and frequency; status (active/suspended/retired/to confirm); scheduler folders and job count; main scripts and procedures; invoked programs (distinguish entry points, routines and encoding variants); application projects; tables read and written; input/output files and layouts; external systems; dependencies through conditions, files or tables; existing AS-IS documentation; S/M/L complexity with explicit criteria (component counts, lines of code, integrations, coupling); open questions. Mark claims [V] verified, [I] inferred or [?] to confirm, and cite source paths.

MANDATORY FINAL SECTIONS: 1) chain summary with counts; 2) reverse index component → chains for programs, application projects and main tables; 3) shared components; 4) unassigned orphan programs, scripts, jobs, projects and tables with counts; 5) reconciliation with EVIDENCE.md totals, explaining every difference; 6) reproducible methodology.

Do not estimate effort or person-days. Do not modify customer material or EVIDENCE.md. Put helper scripts outside customer material in a temporary directory. Write in English.

nodes.title: Adversarial verification (Codex)
nodes.prompt:
Act as an independent adversarial reviewer: seek errors, not confirmation. Read FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md and SUMMARY.md and compare them with actual Source files and EVIDENCE.md.

Check at least: a) a sample of at least 10 chains, or all chains if fewer exist, tracing scheduler folder → job → script/procedure → program → table in primary sources where applicable; b) every scheduler folder, built program, application project and script is assigned to a chain or listed as an orphan; c) totals and reconciliation with EVIDENCE.md; d) unsupported inter-chain dependencies; e) inferences marked [V]; f) nonexistent paths; g) SUMMARY.md numbers that differ from EVIDENCE.md or unsupported claims. Record unavailable checks explicitly.

Create or overwrite CATALOG_REVIEW.md in English. For each finding, state document and section, evidence (source path), blocking/major/minor severity and proposed correction. Do not modify FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md or SUMMARY.md. End with ALIGNED if no blocking or major findings remain, otherwise DIFFERENCES.

nodes.title: Claude refines
nodes.prompt: Read CATALOG_REVIEW.md and any human approval feedback. If the verdict is ALIGNED and there are no blocking or major findings or human requests, change nothing and say so. Otherwise independently check each finding against primary sources: correct FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md or SUMMARY.md with source citations if substantiated; if unfounded, retain the text and explain why. Add or update the Revision log at the end of FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md (finding → action taken). Keep shared numbers consistent in SUMMARY.md. Modify only these two files. Write in English.

nodes.title: Catalog aligned?
nodes.prompt: Compare the current FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md and SUMMARY.md with CATALOG_REVIEW.md findings and actual Source files. Return pass only if each blocking or major finding has been corrected in the files or rejected with verifiable justification and no new significant discrepancies emerge; otherwise return rework for another adversarial verification cycle. Do not approve claimed corrections that are absent from the files. Write the rationale in English.

nodes.title: Final approval
nodes.prompt: Approve SUMMARY.md and FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md. Check the verdict in CATALOG_REVIEW.md and the Revision log. If a correction is needed, choose rework and specify the required changes: the workflow returns to Claude for refinement.

nodes.text:
# Flow
1. **Initial analysis**: reuse a complete EVIDENCE.md if present
2. **SUMMARY.md**: plain-language summary (Claude)
3. **FUNCTIONAL_CATALOG.md**: functional chains (Claude)
4. **Adversarial verification**: Codex writes CATALOG_REVIEW.md
5. **Refinement**: Claude addresses substantiated findings
6. **Codex gate**: pass → human approval; rework → another verification (max 3)
7. **Human approval**: rework → Claude
nodes.title: Notes

workflow.name: Existing software → SDD baseline
workflow.description: Reconstructs current behavior, rules and tests from source and prepares verifiable material for Spec Kit.

nodes.title: Inventory and provenance
nodes.prompt: Read Source and record the commit or file fingerprint, components, languages, dependencies, configurations, entry points and execution instructions in analysis/inventory.md. Do not change application code. Do not read or report secrets.

nodes.title: Architecture and current behavior
nodes.prompt: Reconstruct architecture, flows, data model, APIs, permissions, rules and errors in analysis/as-is.md and analysis/behaviors.md. Cite files and symbols for each conclusion; separate evidence, inference and missing data. Observed behavior is not an approved requirement.

nodes.title: Tests and characterization
nodes.prompt: Inventory and run tests with project tools when available; save commands, results and blockers in analysis/test-baseline.md. Add proportional characterization tests without changing application code. Do not label a suspected defect as a desired requirement. Do not invent coverage or results.

nodes.title: Spec Kit handoff
nodes.prompt: Create analysis/sdd-handoff.md with functional capabilities, Given/When/Then scenarios, candidate criteria, edge cases, constraints, risks and a decision log. Create analysis/traceability.md: behavior → source → test → candidate requirement. Distinguish behavior to preserve, suspected defects and pending decisions. Prepare content usable by Specify/Clarify, Plan and Tasks; do not automatically approve the baseline.

nodes.title: Validate results and open decisions
nodes.prompt: Check artifacts against sources. Distinguish evidence, inference and missing information. Do not turn suspicious behavior into approved requirements. Request outstanding business decisions. No publication or remote changes.

workflow.name: Idea → Approved specification
workflow.description: Clarifies a request and prepares a specification, plan and tasks with Spec Kit before coding.

nodes.title: Constitution
nodes.prompt: Read the project and startup request; define proportional principles and verifiable constraints.

nodes.title: Specify
nodes.prompt: Build the specification from the startup request and sources. If the request is missing, use the Helpdesk case in README. Do not implement.

nodes.title: Clarify
nodes.prompt: Resolve ambiguities using sources; ask for missing business decisions without inventing them.

nodes.title: Plan
nodes.prompt: Prepare a technical plan consistent with the repository and validated requirements.

nodes.title: Tasks and tests
nodes.prompt: Prepare tasks with tests, edge cases and traceable acceptance criteria. Do not implement.

nodes.title: Analyze
nodes.prompt: Check consistency across specification, plan, tasks and planned tests. Document actual blockers.

nodes.title: Validate results and open decisions
nodes.prompt: Check artifacts against sources. Distinguish evidence, inference and missing information. Do not turn suspicious behavior into approved requirements. Request outstanding business decisions. No publication or remote changes.

workflow.name: Feature → SDD → Delivery
workflow.description: Official Spec Kit, real agents, human reviews and local tests. The commit node does not push, merge or deploy. Configure Connection for remote systems.

nodes.title: Constitution
nodes.prompt: Define concise principles: minimal Rust library, no network dependencies, deterministic tests, spec before code. Complete the constitution template and identify necessary questions.

nodes.title: Specify
nodes.prompt: Specify the feature described in README.md: deterministic ticket deduplication. V1 preserves the oldest ticket priority, oldest ID and summed occurrences. Explicitly distinguish the V1 feature from the future V2 request in incident.json. A single feature specs/001-ticket-dedup is sufficient. Do not implement yet.

nodes.title: Clarify
nodes.prompt: Clarify the V1 specification. Follow the rules for all decisions already documented in README. If an actual decision is missing, return needs_input with questions instead of assuming an answer.

nodes.title: Plan
nodes.prompt: Plan the current feature in the existing Rust library. No external services or new dependencies. Use existing artifacts and keep the plan proportional to the repository.

nodes.title: Checklist
nodes.prompt: Check completeness and verifiability of current requirements: ID, fingerprint, priority, occurrences, error cases and tests.

nodes.title: Tasks
nodes.prompt: Generate small, verifiable tasks from the current plan. Include RED/GREEN tests and regressions. Do not rewrite the entire project.

nodes.title: Analyze
nodes.prompt: Analyze consistency across spec, plan and tasks. Explicitly identify blocking gaps; do not claim tests were run at this stage.

nodes.title: Design review
nodes.prompt: Check spec, plan, tasks, checklist and the analyze report. Look for concrete inconsistencies. Ask only for missing decisions; use decision rework for actionable gaps, otherwise pass. Human approval is then required.

nodes.title: Ready for code
nodes.prompt: Confirm that the design review is approved and artifacts agree. Return pass only if no blocking gaps remain, otherwise rework.

nodes.title: Implement
nodes.prompt: Execute all tasks in the current specification. Actually modify files and run cargo test. Keep the library small. Do not push or create PRs; if a test fails, fix it or declare blocked.

nodes.title: Converge
nodes.prompt: Verify actual convergence between implementation and the current spec. Run cargo test; compare acceptance criteria and tasks. Close only tasks actually completed. Return decision pass if convergent, rework if more work is needed.

nodes.title: Convergence verified
nodes.prompt: Check the Converge report and code against the specification. Return pass only if tasks are actually closed and no gaps remain; otherwise rework.

nodes.title: Code review
nodes.prompt: Examine code and actual test evidence. Look for regressions, edge cases and deviations from the current specification. Return decision pass or rework; human approval remains separate.

nodes.title: Quality gate
nodes.prompt: Return pass only with actual passing tests and no blocking gaps in the current review. Do not invent cloud CI or releases.

workflow.name: Incident → Living spec → Delivery
workflow.description: Official Spec Kit, real agents, human reviews and local tests. The commit node does not push, merge or deploy. Configure Connection for remote systems.

nodes.title: Triage SDD
nodes.prompt: Use the skill to assess the repository and existing specification without changing code. Read incident.json. If no initial spec exists, document the V1 behavior described in README as the baseline before classifying. Distinguish implementation defects from specification changes. The preloaded case is a V2 business request eligible for approval, not a bug against V1. decision must be spec_change, code_defect or needs_info.

nodes.title: Classify request
nodes.prompt: Examine the triage report and incident.json. Choose spec_change if a documented business rule changes; code_defect if code violates the current spec; needs_info if facts are missing. Do not infer human approval.

nodes.title: Approve business change
nodes.prompt: Approve V2: oldest ticket and summed occurrences, but lowest numeric priority. A requirement change requires explicit approval.

nodes.title: Update living spec
nodes.prompt: Resume the existing specification: apply the approved V2 business change in incident.json. Update documents only: FR and acceptance criteria for lowest priority, oldest ID, summed occurrences, P1-on-P3 cases and ties. Do not change code or tests in this node: Implement follows planning and review. If Source has no spec.md yet, create a V1 baseline spec.md in specs/001-ticket-dedup, then update that same file to V2, documenting the change. Run the clarify skill on this living spec. Do not use an invented amend command.

nodes.title: Plan
nodes.prompt: Plan the current feature in the existing Rust library. No external services or new dependencies. Use existing artifacts and keep the plan proportional to the repository.

nodes.title: Checklist
nodes.prompt: Check completeness and verifiability of current requirements: ID, fingerprint, priority, occurrences, error cases and tests.

nodes.title: Tasks
nodes.prompt: Generate small, verifiable tasks from the current plan. Include RED/GREEN tests and regressions. Do not rewrite the entire project.

nodes.title: Analyze
nodes.prompt: Analyze consistency across spec, plan and tasks. Explicitly identify blocking gaps; do not claim tests were run at this stage.

nodes.title: Design review
nodes.prompt: Check spec, plan, tasks, checklist and the analyze report. Look for concrete inconsistencies. Ask only for missing decisions; use decision rework for actionable gaps, otherwise pass. Human approval is then required.

nodes.title: Ready for code
nodes.prompt: Confirm that the design review is approved and artifacts agree. Return pass only if no blocking gaps remain, otherwise rework.

nodes.title: Implement
nodes.prompt: Execute all tasks in the current specification. Actually modify files and run cargo test. Keep the library small. Do not push or create PRs; if a test fails, fix it or declare blocked.

nodes.title: Converge
nodes.prompt: Verify actual convergence between implementation and the current spec. Run cargo test; compare acceptance criteria and tasks. Close only tasks actually completed. Return decision pass if convergent, rework if more work is needed.

nodes.title: Convergence verified
nodes.prompt: Check the Converge report and code against the specification. Return pass only if tasks are actually closed and no gaps remain; otherwise rework.

nodes.title: Code review
nodes.prompt: Examine code and actual test evidence. Look for regressions, edge cases and deviations from the current specification. Return decision pass or rework; human approval remains separate.

nodes.title: Quality gate
nodes.prompt: Return pass only with actual passing tests and no blocking gaps in the current review. Do not invent cloud CI or releases.

workflow.name: Evolution → Impact → SDD
workflow.description: Assesses a planned change and prepares specification changes, compatibility and regression tests.

nodes.title: Baseline and impact
nodes.prompt: Read code, specifications and tests. Compare the startup request with the baseline; in the demo use incident.json as a planned evolution. Write analysis/impact.md covering APIs, data, dependencies, compatibility and migration, distinguishing facts from open decisions.

nodes.title: Specification changes
nodes.prompt: Prepare the change specification with before/after behavior, verifiable criteria and requirements to preserve. Do not implement.

nodes.title: Clarify
nodes.prompt: Clarify outstanding business and compatibility decisions.

nodes.title: Evolution plan
nodes.prompt: Prepare a proportional plan with migration and rollback where necessary.

nodes.title: Tasks and regressions
nodes.prompt: Generate tasks with regression tests for behavior to preserve and tests for the change. Do not implement before review.

nodes.title: Consistency
nodes.prompt: Check consistency and traceability of the change, plan and tests.

nodes.title: Validate results and open decisions
nodes.prompt: Check artifacts against sources. Distinguish evidence, inference and missing information. Do not turn suspicious behavior into approved requirements. Request outstanding business decisions. No publication or remote changes.

workflow.name: Jira + GitHub → SDD

nodes.title: Clarify
nodes.prompt: Clarify ticket ambiguities without inventing business decisions.

nodes.title: Plan
nodes.prompt: Prepare the technical plan using the real Source and an appropriate testing strategy.

nodes.title: Tasks
nodes.prompt: Generate verifiable tasks, tests and regressions; prepare delivery/pr-draft.md with traceability and verification criteria. This template ends at plan review: no automatic push, PR or ticket updates.

nodes.title: Analyze
nodes.prompt: Check consistency across ticket, specification, plan, tasks and planned tests.

nodes.title: Validate results and open decisions
nodes.prompt: Check artifacts against sources. Distinguish evidence, inference and missing information. Do not turn suspicious behavior into approved requirements. Request outstanding business decisions. No publication or remote changes.

workflow.name: ServiceNow → Triage and remediation
workflow.description: Links an incident to source code and prepares diagnosis, regression tests and a remediation plan.

nodes.title: Incident triage
nodes.prompt: Compare the incident read from ServiceNow with Source code, specifications and tests. Write analysis/incident.md: evidence, reproduction steps, hypotheses and blockers. Distinguish defects, requirement changes and insufficient information.

nodes.title: Reproduction test
nodes.prompt: Prepare a test reproducing the defect if supported by evidence. Run it and record the actual outcome; do not change application code. If not reproducible, document missing data.

nodes.title: Remediation plan
nodes.prompt: Write delivery/remediation.md with any necessary specification changes, remediation tasks, regressions and a draft ServiceNow note. Distinguish planned, implemented and released fixes from resolved incidents. Do not close or update the remote incident.

nodes.title: Validate results and open decisions
nodes.prompt: Check artifacts against sources. Distinguish evidence, inference and missing information. Do not turn suspicious behavior into approved requirements. Request outstanding business decisions. No publication or remote changes.
